exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal vs. cesarean section)
outcome: Breast milk bacterial phyla composition (Firmicutes, Bacteroidetes, Actinobacteria, Proteobacteria)
cohort: Sixty women participated in the study, with half having had vaginal deliveries and the other half cesarean sections.
finding: The bacterial phyla composition of breast milk was significantly altered by the mode of delivery, and infant sex also influenced the quantity of some phyla.
mod_finding: Breast milk of mothers with cesarean section had significantly higher proportions of Bacteroidetes, Firmicutes, and Proteobacteria, and an increased Firmicutes to Bacteroides ratio, compared to those with vaginal delivery.
